spec.description: Historical weather for one location and date range from reanalysis models, ERA5 by default, hourly and daily, back to 1940.

latitude.description: WGS84 latitude of the location, in degrees.

longitude.description: WGS84 longitude of the location, in degrees.

start_date.description: First day of the range, inclusive.

end_date.description: Last day of the range, inclusive.

hourly.description: Hourly variables to return, such as `temperature_2m`.

daily.description: Daily aggregates to return, such as `precipitation_sum`; they need a `timezone`.

wind_speed_unit.description: Unit for every wind speed variable.

precipitation_unit.description: Unit for precipitation, rain, showers and snowfall.

timeformat.description: How times are rendered: ISO 8601 strings without an offset, local to `timezone`, or Unix seconds in UTC.

timezone.description: IANA time zone the daily aggregates and every ISO 8601 time are expressed in; `auto` resolves the zone of the coordinates.

models.description: Reanalysis models to draw from, such as `era5` or `era5_land`, instead of the automatic best match.

cell_selection.description: Which grid cell serves the coordinates: the nearest land cell, the nearest sea cell, or the nearest of either.

response.description: The location and the requested series.

unverified.detail: No recording yet: the sandbox this spec was written in cannot reach open-meteo.com. The `record.yml` workflow replays `examples/*.request.json` through the generated client with `truewire capture` and opens a pull request with the responses.

notes: The response schema is a subset: it names the fields every response carries and types the series maps. Fields not named here pass through unchecked.

`hourly`, `daily` and `current` are keyed by whichever variables the request asked for, so they are typed as maps rather than records with a fixed field per variable: every value is one column (or one value, for `current`) under the variable name the request used. The `time` column is always there but a map cannot declare one key required.

Times keep the wire type: an ISO 8601 string local to `timezone` with no offset when `timeformat` is `iso8601`, Unix seconds in UTC when it is `unixtime`. Neither is declared as a timestamp format: `date-time` would label a zone-less local time as if it carried one, and a fixed format would reject the other rendering.
A request with several comma-separated coordinates makes the API answer with a JSON array of these objects. That form is not described here; the client takes one location per call.
`apikey` is redacted because the transport adds it to the query on the commercial tier; the free tier sends none.

No pagination block. The API answers a whole date range in one response with no row cap, and the response is columnar (`hourly.time` beside `hourly.temperature_2m`), so a `window` walk over `start_date`/`end_date` would have no row collection to concatenate or to test for emptiness. A caller who wants years of data splits the range.
Reanalysis lags real time by a few days; a range ending at today answers with `null` columns for the missing days.
